description: Deny the conduct. Attack the credibility, motive or stability of the person raising it. Then adopt the victim role and cast the true victim as the offender. Freyd describes it as a particularly pernicious form of denial.
notes: Harsey, Zurbriggen & Freyd, first empirical test 2017.

description: The reversal is persuasive to people with no independent information, because distress is legible and the accused performs distress convincingly.
energy_note: He is upset, visibly, and she is composed.

aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the meeting about the complaint
description: 'I'm honestly shaken by this. I've supported her career for three years.' He is close to tears. 'I don't know what I've done to deserve it.' By the end of the meeting two people have asked whether he is alright and nobody has asked her anything.
energy_note: He cries, and the room reorganises around him.

description: The same pattern performed by an organisation - as when a body responds to a complaint by investigating the complainant. Freyd names it a particularly aggressive form of institutional betrayal.
energy_note: The institution does it too, with a letterhead.
